reference: Ainsworth, S. (2006). DeFT: A conceptual framework for learning with multiple representations. Learning and Instruction, 16(3), 183–198. DOI 10.1016/j.learninstruc.2006.03.001
principal_finding_used: Benefits depend on design parameters, functions served and learner tasks; coordination is itself a cognitive demand.
critical_limit: Framework is not an effectiveness estimate and does not prescribe software architecture.
ARA_implication: Representations must be selected by function and task; more resource types alone are not a quality criterion.

reference: Rexigel et al. (2024). The More the Better? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Benefits of More than Two External Representations in STEM Education. DOI 10.1007/s10648-024-09958-y
principal_finding_used: More than two representations can support performance under some conditions without necessarily increasing time, with effects moderated by support, redundancy and representational configuration.
critical_limit: The comparison does not validate any particular platform or imply that maximal representation count is optimal.
ARA_implication: ARA needs coordination/scaffolding metadata and must test redundancy rather than treat variety as intrinsically beneficial.
source_status: open abstract and article page verified

reference: Ma, W.; Adesope, O. O.; Nesbit, J. C.; Liu, Q. (2014). Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Learning Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis. DOI 10.1037/a0037123
principal_finding_used: ITS outperformed several non-ITS comparison conditions on average, while differences from individual human tutoring and small-group instruction were not significant in the reported synthesis.
critical_limit: ITS is a heterogeneous category and effect estimates depend on comparison conditions and outcome alignment.
ARA_implication: ARA should not claim ITS status or effect merely from interactivity; learner modelling and instructional adaptation require explicit contracts and evaluation.
source_status: ERIC record and author manuscript located

reference: Kulik, J. A.; Fletcher, J. D. (2016). Effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems: A Meta-Analytic Review. DOI 10.3102/0034654315581420
principal_finding_used: Median effects were positive, but evaluation results varied substantially with locally aligned versus standardized outcomes.
critical_limit: Outcome alignment can inflate apparent effectiveness and systems vary widely.
ARA_implication: Research protocols must separate near-transfer measures from independent or standardized outcomes.

reference: Dermeval, D.; Paiva, R.; Bittencourt, I. I.; Vassileva, J.; Borges, D. (2018). Authoring Tools for Designing Intelligent Tutoring Systems: a Systematic Review of the Literature. DOI 10.1007/s40593-017-0157-9
principal_finding_used: Authoring tools chiefly target domain and pedagogical models; non-programmer authoring benefits are reported but tools and technologies are diverse.
critical_limit: Only 33 studies were included and evidence on real-world authoring productivity and quality remains heterogeneous.
ARA_implication: ARA must treat authoring models as first-class and test whether domain experts can author without programming.
source_status: open article and ERIC record verified

reference: Chernikova, O. et al. (2020). Simulation-Based Learning in Higher Education: A Meta-Analysis. DOI 10.3102/0034654320933544
principal_finding_used: Simulation can support complex-skill learning, with scaffolding type and technology among important design dimensions.
critical_limit: Simulation studies and tasks are heterogeneous; an interactive animation is not automatically a simulation.
ARA_implication: A simulation capability needs model variables
column9: scaffolding and outcome probes rather than a visual renderer alone.

reference: de Jong, T.; Linn, M. C.; Zacharia, Z. C. (2013). Physical and Virtual Laboratories in Science and Engineering Education. DOI 10.1126/science.1230579
principal_finding_used: Physical and virtual investigations have distinct and potentially complementary affordances.
critical_limit: Short selective review; does not justify replacing all physical practice with virtual environments.
ARA_implication: ARA virtual-lab components must state which phenomena and practices they represent and what remains outside the environment.

reference: Çeken, B.; Taşkın, N. (2022). Multimedia learning principles in different learning environments: a systematic review. DOI 10.1186/s40561-022-00200-2
principal_finding_used: Multimedia principles are context-sensitive and have been studied across different learning environments.
critical_limit: The multimedia label covers varied designs and does not imply that video is required.
ARA_implication: ARA may coordinate verbal and graphical representations while remaining text/JSON-centred; video is not entailed by multimedia theory.

reference: Alhadi, M.; Zhang, D.; Wang, T.; Maher, C. A. (2023). Digitalized Interactive Components in Computer-Based Assessment in Mathematics for K–12 Students. DOI 10.1080/07380569.2022.2116622
principal_finding_used: The small literature includes language assistance and response-construction supports rather than only conventional selected response.
critical_limit: Only ten studies were found and populations/constructs were unevenly represented.
ARA_implication: Construction and accessibility supports should be investigated as assessment design features
column9: institutional abstract and bibliographic record verified

reference: Tang, X.; Yin, Y.; Lin, Q.; Hadad, R.; Zhai, X. (2020). Assessing computational thinking: A systematic review of empirical studies. DOI 10.1016/j.compedu.2019.103798
principal_finding_used: Assessment types include programming/computing tasks, traditional assessments, portfolios and disposition surveys; validity evidence is uneven.
critical_limit: Computational thinking is contested and measures often cover different constructs.
ARA_implication: ARA must not infer a single programming/CT construct from code execution events; tasks and evidence need construct definitions.

reference: Messer, M.; Brown, N. C. C.; Kölling, M.; Shi, M. (2023). Automated Grading and Feedback Tools for Programming Education: A Systematic Review. arXiv:2306.11722
principal_finding_used: Unit tests and static analysis dominate; feedback is often limited to pass/fail, expected/actual output or reference-solution differences.
critical_limit: Preprint status and heterogeneous evaluation methods; broad tool corpus does not establish learning effects.
ARA_implication: Execution is insufficient: ARA needs diagnostic feedback layers and should evaluate code quality dimensions separately from correctness.

reference: Gao, R.; Merzdorf, H. E.; Anwar, S.; Hipwell, M. C.; Srinivasa, A. (2023). Automatic assessment of text-based responses in post-secondary education: A systematic review. arXiv:2308.16151
principal_finding_used: Automated text assessment spans many models, inputs and outcomes and may support rapid feedback at scale.
source_status: transparency and domain transfer remain variable; model scoring is not deterministic equivalence.
column9: Probabilistic assistance must be separated from authoritative grading and combined with rubrics

reference: Buitrago, M.; Chiappe, A. (2019). Representation of Knowledge in Digital Educational Environments: A Systematic Review of Literature. Australasian Journal of Educational Technology, 35(4), 46–62
domain_or_scope: knowledge representation in digital educational environments
principal_finding_used: Knowledge-representation systems support varied cognitive and metacognitive purposes and use multiple instruments.
critical_limit: The field is broad and the review does not supply a ready software ontology.
ARA_implication: ARA resource discovery should include knowledge-representation literature beyond flashcards and multimedia widgets.

reference: Permatasari, M. B.; Rahayu, S.; Dasna, I. W. (2022). Chemistry Learning Using Multiple Representations: A Systematic Literature Review. Journal of Science Learning, 5(2), 334–341
principal_finding_used: Chemistry learning requires coordination of macro, submicroscopic and symbolic representations.
critical_limit: Only eleven articles were included and review quality/details require full-text appraisal.
ARA_implication: A reaction equation is only one chemistry grammar; future chemistry capabilities must coordinate levels of representation when the objective demands it.

reference: Fagerlund, J.; Häkkinen, P.; Vesisenaho, M.; Viiri, J. (2021). Computational thinking in programming with Scratch in primary schools: A systematic review. DOI 10.1002/cae.22255
principal_finding_used: Block-based programming activities support several computational-thinking practices but definitions and assessments vary.
critical_limit: Primary-school/Scratch focus limits transfer to all programming and professional contexts.
ARA_implication: Blockly-like construction is a candidate interaction engine
source_status: not a universal programming pedagogy or assessment model.

reference: Shute, V. J. (2008). Focus on Formative Feedback. DOI 10.3102/0034654307313795
principal_finding_used: Feedback effectiveness depends on task, content, timing and learner conditions; more informative feedback often outperforms bare verification.
critical_limit: Broad review and heterogeneous interventions; principles are not direct product defaults.
source_status: feedback content and feedback timing must remain separate configurable layers.
